newsitem.title: USA: Woman jailed for Thai prostitution ring in Calif..
newsitem.headline: Woman jailed for Thai prostitution ring in Calif..

text.p: The head of a crime ring that smuggled women into the United States from Thailand to work as prostitutes has been sentenced to 21 months in prison by a federal judge, U.S. prosecutors said Tuesday.
The U.S. Attorney's office said Kalaya Dolatre, 42, was sentenced on Monday in Santa Ana, California, by U.S. District Court Judge Linda McLaughlin.
Dolatre had pleaded guilty in September to one count of conspiracy to import illegal aliens for the purpose of prostitution.
Assistant U.S. Attorney David Lavine said Dolatre and an assistant Thuc Khanh Do operated a brothel in an apartment in the Los Angeles suburb of Westminster.
Do pleaded guilty last year to conspiracy and was sentenced to five months in prison and five months in a community corrections centre.

According to prosecutors, Dolatre arranged for women to be recruited in Thailand and to enter the United States with false documents. The women lived in her apartment and worked as prostitutes to pay off their smuggling fee, Lavine said.
Dolatre paid the women a subsistence allowance on which to live, he said.
